Law Passed: Colorado HB22-1355 (Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act), signed June 3, 2022, covering all packaging materials and paper products (including poly bags, plastic film, paper, and other flexible/rigid packaging). The program entered active implementation as of January 1, 2026, with producer dues obligations live. Within the last 30 days, the ILMA lawsuit against CDPHE (filed March 12, 2026) remains pending in Denver District Court with no injunction in place, and SB26-192 (EPR dues appeal bill) was introduced in the 2026 session but did not advance to enactment before the legislature adjourned May 13, 2026.
Status Detail: Colorado's EPR program is fully live: producers of all covered packaging and paper products have been required to register with CAA since October 2024, submit supply reports (2024 data due July 31, 2025; 2025 data due May 31, 2026), and pay annual dues beginning January 2026. CDPHE approved CAA's final program plan on December 9, 2025, with CAA required to begin full implementation by June 9, 2026. A legal challenge by the Independent Lubricant Manufacturers Association (ILMA) filed March 12, 2026 in Denver District Court alleges constitutional and statutory violations in CDPHE's program implementation; no injunction has been issued and the program continues to operate.

Law Passed: Connecticut has no enacted EPR packaging law. Two successive packaging EPR-related bills failed to advance: HB 6917 (2025 session) died on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, and HB 5151 (2026 session) died in committee. Connecticut's 2026 legislative session has adjourned without passing packaging EPR legislation.
Status Detail: HB 6917, a solid-waste omnibus bill that included a mandate to study the need and viability of packaging EPR by January 15, 2027, passed the House in the 2025 session but was tabled on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, the final day of session, and died there. In the 2026 session, HB 5151—introduced February 11, 2026—would have required the state to submit EPR program proposals derived from a waste characterization study, but it died in committee before the 2026 session ended. A separate packaging-related bill, HB 5524 (polystyrene and PFAS-straw ban), also died in committee in the 2026 session. Connecticut has enacted a postconsumer recycled content requirement for plastic beverage containers (HB 6664, 2023) and an EPR law for consumer batteries (HB 5019, 2025), but no comprehensive packaging EPR program.
